Subject: Serious Concern About Cheating in CS2 – Ruining the Experience for New Players

Dear CS2 Development Team,

I am writing to express my frustration and disappointment with the current state of cheating in Counter-Strike 2.

As a new player trying to get into the game, my experience has been extremely frustrating. It feels like around 70% of the matches I play involve suspicious players, particularly people seemingly using wallhacks (WH) and other cheats.

It's incredibly discouraging to spend time learning the game, improving my aim, understanding maps, and trying to enjoy competitive matches, only to feel like I'm constantly playing against people who have an unfair advantage.

How is a new player supposed to enjoy CS2 or stay motivated to improve when cheating seems so common? It's ruining the competitive experience, destroying fair gameplay, and pushing potential new players away from the game.

I strongly urge the CS2 team to take this issue more seriously by:

Improving the anti-cheat system and cheat detection.
Taking faster action against confirmed cheaters.
Improving the reporting system and follow-up on reports.
Prioritizing fair matchmaking, especially for new players.
Counter-Strike has an incredible legacy, and CS2 has the potential to be one of the best competitive games out there. But without fair matches, none of that matters.

Please don't let cheaters drive away new players before they even get the chance to fall in love with the game.

I genuinely want to enjoy CS2, improve, and become part of the community, but the current experience makes that extremely difficult.

I hope this feedback reaches the right people and leads to meaningful improvements.

Best regards,
A frustrated new CS2 player who genuinely wants to enjoy the game.

review:
As of 2026 the game is more dead than FragPunk and the devs have left the game in favor of development on Deadlock, minus the 30 people assigned to CS2 who clearly either don't play the game or refuse to tell their superiors the true state of the game so long as money is coming in. Updates to the game are added a year or two in advance and then just left ready to patch in when player numbers drop, like the recent 'pet chicken update' which has been ready and stable for ages yet Valve has a habit of making content for seemingly no reason and then they'll just randomly drop it one day when they've decided they need a player boost.

If you're playing NAE or EU this year, even with a perfect reputation and in-game Green Trust Factor, you'll find it's almost impossible to find a game with ten legit players anymore, because cheating is simply ignored, and in-game drops are based on exp that's founded on Rounds Won and not performance. Valve's own mechanics promote cheating to farm as many items as you can from their Weekly Drops or Armory Pass systems. No matter how much the community complains or pro players alert Valve, they don't care, and their previous two "major actions" essentially boiled down to "Half of our player base are now item-farming bots. We should remove the rare and expensive Weekly Drop items" and "The top players in our seasonal leaderboard are all well known hackers and bots. Delete the Leaderboard function from the game". You'll find in these regions VAC is basically useless even when they claim to have a large wave of bans, as Valve's priority seems to be keeping as many Eastern European players as possible, as their poor national states gives rise to gambling and engaging with Valve's systems. I know people on both sides of the Russia/Ukraine war who've taken to cheating and selling accounts because it's a way of making money while their homes go to crap and Valve profits from having "an active playerbase" and players engaging with the market, where they take a cut.

The game functions mostly as a case-opening gambling simulator, but even then the Market is down so badly (roughly 25-50% of stable item prices have been cut off) because legitimate players are a slim fraction of the population now. You'd think now is a good time to buy said items but every day we see more and more players leaving and uninstalling because once you've left and moved on, the sunk cost nonsense goes away. You may as well save your items for the day maybe the game is good, and save your money not buying items for a game you should leave. Valve introduced "a friendlier gambling option" with their Terminal system that's supposed to offer skins at around market price, however the items offered are always cheaper from the market (in better condition too) and are significantly cheaper-for-better on third-party sites (often the price of a beaten up terminal item will get you the same item pristine, or nearly pristine online). These systems exist just to silence government anti-gambling agencies and to get money from countries who cannot use said third-party sites and are relegated to the Steam Community Market. They're not balanced or honest and, like most of the game's practices, exist only to tax the stupid and the 'geographically-handicapped' as Valve would call it.

If you have any maps or skins in the game, which I don't personally but my boyfriend does, you'll likely know that the Workshop function has changed drastically too. Not only are the maps and skins player-made but they're now paid on a fixed-rate basis and not as a percentage of sales. This is fine for mappers as that's a one-and-done thing but for skin creators they've basically nuked 90% of the revenue you would have received (and those older players have received) for a stable palming-off price they can shut you up with, especially as they've not yet removed gambling or cases at all, so previous collections still see their creators paid significantly more. This is fine for anyone who already had work in the game but they're basically asking current and future users to design maps and skins for their game that's already on life support, for little reward, certainly compared to the older, better skin creators, and hoping that nobody asks them questions about their own pay. Older creators still get their monthly pay but anyone getting into it now won't get more than a small cheque and probably not even a thanks.

Events are over. We used to get seasonal events, in-game items, stream rewards, souvenirs, etc. Since CS2 has launched there's been nothing. No Operations, though since the playerbase seems barely legitimate anymore you can understand Valve not making large updates that requires models and voice lines anymore. Even worse though, while the game gets an update every few days to a week, to update coding and allow better Community Updates, there is no CS2 Community. All the major servers and CSGO scenes are gone, and have not, and will not, come back. Sure we have Surf, KZ, and BHop servers, but CSGO had full working ports of all the classic CSS maps and modes. Simpsons Gungame, Decoy Dodgeball, Zombies, Prop Hunt, Lego modes (though 1v1 Lego AWP Arena exists still), Hide and Seek, the various horror modes that weren't just zombie wave maps, kart racing, etc. They're all gone, and most of those communities have stated they're not looking to come back. A big one was UKCS but a bunch of NA community scenes over here all retired their servers after CSGO died. Valve keeps updating the game to make community things easier to make and run but there's nobody left who wants it, and it seems like those updates are to CS2 what Forge was to Halo Infinite. Yeah the toolkit is cool but the game is dead and nobody will ever truly engage with it, besides maybe mappers wanting their easy 30 grand for a game they won't play.


If you don't have the game already, there's better alternatives out there. If you wanna play with bots and maybe revive a better game, go save FragPunk. If you want the CS gameplay with abilities and skins, play Valorant. If you just want simple CS gunplay and a military motif, I can think of at least three superior games on Steam, but also just go back to CS:S. 
The devs don't care about the true state of the game, beyond that it's making them millions monthly. The community scene is all dead outside of a few modes. In-game creators have been shafted because Valve wants as much money as possible before they're forced to remove gambling entirely. There's nothing in CS2 that wasn't either better in Source or Global Offensive, and there's little left in CS that hasn't been done better by companies who don't hate you as much as Valve does. Save yourself the headache and play better.

review:
Genuinely one of the most unfriendly games for new players ive ever tried. I spent several evenings trying to get to grips with this because I liked the idea of drop-in drop-out gameplay with a high skill ceiling that rewarded investment.

I tried deathmatch, only to get head-tapped by AKs with frame-perfect reactions. I read a bit and it turns out deathmatch/casual isnt good because its swarmed by bots running scripts to farm kills for experience and crates. Okay whatever I unlocked competitive, thats like the ranked thing isnt it? So I'll be able to play with people around my skill level? I won maybe one game out of a full fifteen, the one that I won was because the other team literally had a player disconnect, every other game wasn't close either, like blowouts every time. Read some more and it turns out the matchmaking is so poor that most games are completely one-sided, driven by one or two players playing several times better than anyone else farming kills, which was exactly my experience. Okay, dunno why its called competitive then, but someone in one of these games told me Premiere is probably more my speed. Awesome! Oh wait, nevermind, after a literal entire calendar day of playing Im only 30% of the way to unlocking that mode.

Practice isnt the solution, and saying otherwise is an excuse to offload the labor of onboarding new players. Everywhere I look I'm being told to "embrace the suck and practice", but practice modes with bots dont get me out of lobbies full of people that have been playing for a lifetime longer than I have and can hit frame-perfect AWP headshots in their sleep; And telling a new player "it sucks for the first hundred hours then you maybe get kinda good" feels braindead when the market for competitive shooters is as flooded as its ever been. There's a million options that respect my time, why choose the option that feels like it goes out of its way to be hostile?

A functioning match-making system to group the people that can hit frame-perfect AWP headshots and people like me separately shouldnt be beyond this billion-dollar corporation, or the game modes that provide that shouldnt be so separate. You can tell this game has been around for literal generations, and that the average player is a returning player. In loading in for the first time you're inundated with menus (and opportunities to purchase cosmetics, gross), with next to zero real explanation for what anything is. When you're designing a product under the assumption that the average user has been using it for a lifetime already, you dont think about new players. Thats exactly whats happened with this game, and you feel it every hour the game's running. It feels like I'm missing a thousand hours of context before I should even be able to launch.

0/10, will be actively rooting for CS2's downfall

review:
Counter Strike always had been a good game
I started playing 1.6 with my cousin when i was ~5 to 6 years old on zombie mode made by community, Same for counter strike source

I loved watching those videos of players recording themselves playing those gamemodes, it was very entertaining and I am very happy to have Counter Strike as a part of my childhood

Same for csgo that was a banger, i remember hitting a 7vs1 with awp on awp lego servers 
There was this feeling of comfort that Counter Strike 2 will never get

Sure there was a lot of cheaters, this is without any doubt, probably we would see them less often due to the massive amount of game modes, but there was overwatch, an anti-cheat that was not perfect, but did the job, the bhop felt nice, the physic felt nice, animation were smooth and no problem at all

Today, the game is full of cheaters, premier, competitive, rush, wingman, casual every mode includes cheaters at a very high rate

I did not mention cheaters in deathmatch because there isn't a single cheater there, except for bots who their only objective is to farm weekly care package for cases (alias money)

It was so bad that Valve had to remove the good drops (CSGO weapon case 1, 2 and bravo case)

Spinbotters in premier will make you leave the game sooner that you came in, one game you win 150 elo, the next spinbotters that will make you lose between 200 and 450 elo 

Valve is not even doing the skins anymore, or maps, it's just a rotation of community maps, same for game modes and operations

The game lacks of content, and you feel it when Valve adds chickens instead of fixing real problems

Animgraph2 popped up on AK, AWP, SCOUT, M4A4, M4A1-S, and most of them got wiped out for no reason (at least they were not given) when they were nice.

The game's physic is not perfect, when cs2 released it was horribly bad, and was like the player got 50kg added on his body (It got improved today, but it's still not like CSGO)

The optimizations could be done better, same for the storage, at the moment cs2 is about ~75gb if I am not mistaken when CSGO was 35gb MAX (If I am not wrong)

TL:DR :

- Anti cheat needs improvement
- New content needed (Old game modes back, operations or even weapons)
- A better physic for movements like strafe jumps or such
- Better Optimizations (on some animations like pull outs, or even FPS opti)
- Do not touch with people's trust (Random update that makes -2 billion$ on the global market)
- Put the old ban map system on premier
- Put the old point system to 16, and an option for 13 rounds in case people wants short matches
- Fix the Tab bug, when pressing tab the game freezes shortly, or does insane FPS drops (or it gives FPS boost when low FPS for some people)

Thanks for reading all that, sorry for the spelling mistakes (I won't ask slop gpt to correct them)

review:
Not Recommended — Legitimate Players Get Punished While Cheaters Remain

It's hard to recommend a competitive game when you can get punished despite never cheating.

I received a 20-hour cooldown after VAC flagged my gameplay as irregular. When the cooldown expired, I gave the game another chance, only to have my very first match disrupted and receive a 7-day cooldown. I have never used cheats, and I even tried closing background applications to rule out potential software conflicts.

Meanwhile, encountering suspected cheaters in actual matches remains frustrating. It feels backwards when legitimate players end up afraid to play because of repeated anti-cheat detections they cannot explain.

I'm not claiming that every VACNET detection is wrong, but legitimate players deserve transparency, a reliable way to appeal potential false positives, and confidence that they won't risk escalating penalties without understanding why.

I absolutely LOVE Counter-Strike 2. ...So why don't I recommend it?

I think it's a great game, considering the rough start after CS:GO. Before the skins and gambling, CS actually felt like a very competitive skill game. The amount of so called content creators on YouTube that actually create multiple full length video's each week about new skins and changes etc. really made me realize that CS:GO, and now CS2 had became a casual FPS game that has now reached a whole extra audience that only care about digital pixels. With these skins and stuff, I feel it's more about the inventory than it is about the actual skill. 

But this wasn't my biggest concern, and not the reason I do not recommend this game. I almost never write reviews, but as they say in elections, every vote counts, ..this is my vote. Although it's just one simple man's opinion, this game is not playable or enjoyable any longer due to the amount of cheaters  in this game. The situation has became really, really bad. To every dedicated player that made it this far in my review, thank you, please consider writing a review yourself as a signal to Valve to let them know that we are fed up with the lack of attention to this matter. 

Peace.
